Born about 1586 at Marefield, Leicestershire, and educated at Cambridge.
A Puritan preacher at Chelmsford, Essex, he was driven out by Archbishop Laud and fled to the Netherlands,
then came to Massachusetts on the Griffin in 1633 and became minister at Newtown,
now Cambridge. In 1636 he led his congregation a hundred miles through the wilderness to found Hartford,
and his preaching is credited with inspiring the Fundamental Orders of Connecticut in 1639.
He died at Hartford on 7 July 1647, in an epidemic.
Susanna, wife of the Reverend Thomas Hooker; she went with him to the Netherlands,
to New England in 1633 and to Hartford in 1636.
Her surname is still argued over. Her daughter Sarah married the Reverend John Wilson of Medfield.
